title: US Air Force responds to suspected drone activity over UK airbase | CNN
text:
Source: Reuters

US Air Force personnel at the RAF Lakenheath base in Britain responded to “suspected unauthorized drone activity” on Friday evening, although no personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected, a US Air Force spokesperson said.

“We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors, and all of our families,” the spokesperson said by email.

Britain’s Ministry of Defence said US Air Force Security Forces personnel had responded to reports of unauthorized drone activity and that the situation had been resolved.

“We are working closely with them to establish the facts. We will provide updates in due course,” a ministry spokesperson said in an emailed statement.

The US has in recent weeksmoved bombersthat had been used to strike Iran out of Britain, and relocated huge refueling aircraft from Britain to Germany. A news report later said there had been a threat from Iran.

The bombers leftRAF Fairfordon security grounds after a group of men approached ​the base in white vans in the middle of the night on September 27.

Two men ​were charged last month in relation to ⁠that incident, with prosecutors alleging one of them had tried to assist Iranian intelligence in Britain. The US Justice Department said this week that a member of an Iran-backed militia had plotted to attack the Fairford air base while detained in the US on criminal charges.

The Wall Street Journal has reported that the refueling aircraft were moved due to a threat from Iran.

Britain’s domestic spy ‌chief said in October that Iran had stepped up attempts tohit ​harder targets such as military sitesin Britain.

Tehran has rejected accusations of involvement in the Fairford incident or any other accusations of malign activity in Britain, where the authorities have ​for a number of years accused it of being involved in plots and attempted assassinations against dissidents and Israeli and Jewish targets.

Germany hasblamed Russiafor an attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport in August after airport workers found a drone laden with explosives and a detonator at the airport, an important civilian freight and NATO logistics hub in eastern Germany that is also a base for several giant Ukrainian Antonov An-124 cargo planes.
